newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police chief in Cools murder probe resigns.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police chief in Cools murder probe resigns.

text.p: One of the chief police investigators into the murder of Belgian politician Andre Cools five years ago resigned on Sunday, the Belgian judiciary said.

"In the light of new developments in the Cools investigation and the doubts expressed by some regarding the professional integrity of chief commissioner Raymond Brose, he has informed us he no longer wishes to be part of the investigative team," the public prosecutor of the city of Liege, Anne Thily, said in a communique published by national news agency Belga.
The resignation followed reports on Belgian televison earlier on Sunday which criticised Brose's professional conduct in the five-year old investigation.
Cools was murdered on July 18, 1991. The investigation into the assassination has uncovered a series of corruption scandals in Belgium, but Cools' killer has not yet been found.
Earlier on Sunday the Liege judiciary arrested former regional minister Alain Van der Biest in connection with the murder. His former secretary and three others were arrested on Friday.
